name: Cache
location: Firefox: Cache (older) / cache2 (Firefox 32+) folder under the profile ; Chrome/Edge: Cache\ folder under the profile (data_# index files and f_###### content files)
purpose: Local storage of web page components (images, scripts, stylesheets, media) retained to speed up subsequent visits to the same site.
key_fields: Cached file content (data_#/f_###### or cache2 entries)
normal_baseline: Cache contains component files from routinely visited, work-appropriate sites, refreshed on a normal schedule as pages are revisited.
anomalies: Cached page content or images matching known phishing kits, C2 panels, or malicious payload delivery pages
Cache entries for a site with no corresponding History record, indicating History was cleared while Cache was left intact
Cached executable or script content served from an otherwise benign-looking domain
anti_forensic_notes: Cache is typically cleared separately from History in browser "clear data" dialogs unless a user explicitly selects it, so an emptied History with an intact Cache (or vice versa) is common — each should be checked independently.
interpretation: Cache provides a genuine snapshot in time of what a user was looking at, including the literal files rendered (images, scripts) rather than just a URL reference — useful for confirming exactly what content a page displayed at a given moment. It is tied to the specific local user account whose profile holds it, and its two timestamps (first-saved vs. last-viewed) can separate a one-time visit from repeated return visits.
